questions.question: By selling 40 dozen bananas for ₹ 1,440, a man gains 20%. In order to gain 30%, for how much should he sell 20 dozen bananas ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling Price of 40 dozen bananas is Rs.1440

Gain % = 20%

**Formula used:**

Profit (P) = SP - CP

CP = SP/(100 + Gain%) × 100

SP = CP/100 × (100 + Gain%), where

SP = Selling price

CP = Cost price

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

SP of 40 dozen bananas = Rs.1440 and profit % = 20%

CP = 1440/(100 + 20) × 100

⇒ CP = 1440/120 × 100 

⇒ CP = 1200

CP of 40 dozen bananas = Rs.1200

CP of 20 dozen bananas = 1200/2 = Rs.600

SP of 20 dozen bananas for 30% gain

⇒ SP = 600/100 × 130

⇒ SP = Rs.780

**∴ To get 30% gain, he should sell 20 dozen bananas for Rs.780.**

questions.question: If the difference between the selling prices of an article when sold at 18% discount and at 10.5% discount is Rs. 192, then the marked price of the article is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount percentages are 18% and 10.5%

**Concept used:**

SP = MP - MP × Discount%

**Calculation:**

Let marked price be 100x

So,

SP = 100x - 18x = 82x [When Discount = 18%]

SP = 100x - 10.5x = 89.5x [When Discount = 10.5%]

According to the question,

89.5x - 82x = 192

⇒ 7.5x = 192

⇒ 100x = 2560

**∴ The marked price of the article is Rs.2560**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** 18% - 10.5% = 192

⇒ 7.5% = 192

⇒ 1% = 25.6

⇒ Marked price = 100% = 100 × 25.6 = Rs. 2560

questions.question: An article was subject to three successive discounts, whereby a customer had to pay ₹ 2,366.8 less than the marked price of ₹ 12,500. If the rates of the first two discounts were, respectively, 12% and 6%, then what was the rate percentage of the third discount?

Using successive multiplying factors: 12500 × 0.88 × 0.94 × (1 − d/100) = 10133.2

⇒ 10340 × (1 − d/100) = 10133.2

Third discount value = 10340 − 10133.2 = 206.8

Third discount % = (206.8 ÷ 10340) × 100 = 2%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two or more discounts are applied sequentially on the Marked Price, they are called successive discounts. The formula for effective discount of two successive discounts d₁ and d₂ is: D = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Selling Price Formula

For a sequence of three discounts d₁%, d₂%, and d₃%, the Final Selling Price is given by: SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100).

Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP)

Marked Price is the listed price of the article. Selling Price is the price at which it is actually sold after applying all discounts. Discount = MP − SP.

questions.question: A dealer sells an article by allowing a 15% discount on its marked price and gains 12%. If the cost price of the article is increased by 10%, how much discount percentage should he allow now on the same marked price so as to earn the same percentage profit as before?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount = 15%

Gains = 12%

**Formula used:**

Discount % = (M.P – S.P)/M.P × 100

**Calculation:**

Let C.P of an article be 100 unit

⇒ For 12% profit S.P = 112 unit

15% discount on mark price

⇒ S.P = 85% = 112 unit

⇒ M.P = 100% = ?

⇒ M.P = (100 × 112)/85

⇒ M.P = 2240/17

If C.P increased by 10%

⇒ New C.P = 110 unit

⇒ For 12% profit new S.P = (110 × 112)/100

⇒ 616/5

Discount % = (M.P – S.P)/M.P × 100

⇒ (2240/17 – 616/5)/(2240/17) × 100

⇒ 6.5%

**∴ The discount percentage should be allowed now on the same marked price is 6.5%**

questions.question: Three articles are bought at Rs.180 each. One of them is sold at a loss of 10%. If the other two articles are sold so as to gain 25% on the whole transaction, then what is the gain percentage on the two articles?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of three articles = Rs. 180 each

Loss = 10%

Gain = 25% 

**Formula used:**

Gain = SP – CP

Gain% = Gain/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

CP of three articles = Rs. (180 × 3) = Rs. 540

Total gain% on whole transaction = 25%

So, 

SP of the three articles = Rs. (540 × 125/100)

⇒ Rs. 675

SP of the first article = Rs. (180 × 90)/100 

⇒ Rs. 162

CP of the other two articles = Rs. (180 × 2) = Rs. 360

SP of the other two articles = Rs. (675 – 162) = Rs. 513

Gain on two articles =Rs. (513 – 360) = Rs. 153

Gain% on the two articles = (153/360 × 100)

⇒ (15,300/360)

⇒ 42.5%

**∴ The required gain% on the two articles is 42.5%**

questions.question: Raghu bought some pens at the rate of 12 for ₹100 and an equal number of pens at 15 for ₹135. How many pens should he sell for ₹260, so as to make a profit of 20%?

**Concept Used:**

In such questions,

Assume the total number of articles purchased is the LCM of the given rate

⇒ Cost of 180 pens (12 ×15) = 135 × 12 = Rs.1620

⇒ Total cost of (180 + 180) of 360 pens = 1500 + 1620 = Rs. 3120

Total cost of 360 pens = Rs. 3120

⇒ The cost of 1 pen = 3120/360

Total cost price = 260 times ((100)/(100 + 20))

⇒ Number of pens = 25

**∴ 25 pens can be purchased in Rs. 260**

questions.question: A man sells 30 apples for the cost price of 40 apples. His profit percentage (correct to two places of decimal) is :
questions.solution:
**Given:**

SP of 30 apples = CP of 40 apples

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP – CP

Profit% = Profit/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

SP of 30 apples = CP of 40 apples

⇒ SP/CP = 4/3

Profit = (4 – 3) = 1

Profit% = (1/3 × 100)

⇒ 100/3%

⇒ 33.33%

**∴ The profit percentage is 33.33%**
